primary_claim: The standard Attack Success Rate (ASR) metric drastically overstates the effectiveness of backdoor-removal techniques (attention-head ablation and 'backdoor vector' subtraction) from Backdoor Attribution (2025): using a richer output-quality metric (Good/Strange/Wrong/Refused) instead of exact-string matching, ablation success on Llama-2-7B-Chat drops from ~30% to ~1%, the backdoor-vector approach drops from 75% to 28% ASR-equivalent reduction on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and from 95% to 46% on Llama-2-7B-Chat, ASR also picks the wrong intervention layer, and ablation shows an 'alignment tax' degrading normal-input performance at or below the head-count needed to suppress the backdoor.

effect.metric: Behavioral Attack Success Rate (BASR) vs original ASR reduction
effect.value: backdoor vector: ASR reduction 75%->BASR 28% (Qwen2.5); 95%->46% (Llama-2); ablation: ASR-based 30% success -> new-metric ~1% success (Llama-2); best layer per ASR (layer 20) is worse than layer 11 by new metric (10x more good answers, >2x fewer refusals)

contradicts_or_qualifies: Backdoor Attribution: Elucidating and Controlling Backdoors in Language Models (arXiv:2509.21761), whose ASR-based evaluation the author reproduces successfully but argues substantially overstates real-world backdoor removal effectiveness and misidentifies the optimal intervention layer
stated_future_work: Improve initial backdoor training using higher-quality or model-generated synthetic datasets to minimize unintended capability alteration
Try full fine-tuning instead of LoRA for backdoor injection to see if it affects removal technique results
Investigate trigger generalization and how removal techniques affect triggering on semantically related (non-exact) inputs
Try alternative ablation methods (e.g. setting heads to mean activation rather than zero)
Construct backdoor vectors using mechanistic interpretability or representation engineering techniques other than CIE
limitations_stated: The BASR metric does not detect cases where a backdoor replaces a previously wrong answer with another wrong answer
The hypothesis that ablating 1 head improves performance by removing SFT-induced degradation has low confidence and needs further analysis
Alignment-tax finding may be model-specific and may not generalize to larger or more capable models
quote: A backdoor removal technique that looks 95% effective by the standard metric may only be 46% effective in reality, and for another technique, what looks like 30% success is actually 1%.
